name: How do I renovate a living space without making the home feel smaller?

mainEntity.name: What design choices help a living room or family room feel bigger during a renovation, especially in smaller Los Angeles homes?
mainEntity.text: What design choices help a living room or family room feel bigger during a renovation, especially in smaller Los Angeles homes?

acceptedAnswer.text: A room does not need more square footage to feel larger. The most effective choices usually improve light, circulation, and visual continuity. That means reducing unnecessary partitions, keeping flooring consistent across connected spaces, and choosing finishes that do not chop the room into small zones. Built-ins can help with storage, but oversized cabinetry or heavy millwork can make a space feel cramped if overused. Lighting placement matters too: layered lighting, dimmers, and brighter ambient light can dramatically change the feel of a room. Homeowners should also think carefully about furniture scale and traffic paths. A renovation plan that maximizes openness and storage at the same time usually creates the most comfortable result. If the room has low ceilings or limited windows, a designer should be involved early to avoid design choices that unintentionally close the space in.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use light colors, continuous flooring, better lighting, fewer visual breaks, and furniture scaled to the room. Avoid overcrowding the space with bulky built-ins, heavy trim, or too many finish changes. Opening sightlines and improving natural light usually makes the biggest difference in how large a room feels.
